blocks.heading: Why research matters
blocks.text: Market research collects and analyses information relevant to a market decision, such as customer needs, demand, competitors or preferences. It can reduce uncertainty before committing resources, guide a suitable offering and review whether existing customers are satisfied. It does not guarantee success. A biased sample, outdated information or leading question can create misleading confidence. Start with the decision and information needed, choose appropriate sources, collect and analyse evidence, then assess its limitations before acting. A stated willingness to buy is not an actual order. Research is part of marketing, not the whole process of designing and supplying an offering.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Fictional Omi Lunches wants to choose a meal format before buying specialised packaging. Asking relevant prospective buyers about preferred formats and feasible prices can reduce the risk of buying unwanted packaging. Interviewing only the owner’s friends would weaken the evidence if they do not represent the intended customers.
